result.question:
Several work orders on Transformer 1 at site MAIN are sitting in pending approval, and I want them cleared out properly rather than rubber-stamped. Pull every pending-approval work order on Transformer 1 and give me each one's number, description, priority, reported date and any failure code. Then check the latest oil sample and run a dissolved gas fault classification on it. Use the five fault gases (hydrogen, methane, ethane, ethylene and acetylene), and use co to check whether the paper is involved.

Sort each pending work order into one of three outcomes:
- Approve it if its description matches the fault the gases currently indicate, or if it is a routine oil sampling job.
- Cancel it if another open or pending work order on Transformer 1 already covers the same job. Keep the older one, cancel the newer one, and put the older work order's number in the cancellation reason.
- Otherwise, leave it pending and tell me in one sentence why.

For any work order you approve that deals with arcing, discharge or tap changer work, raise its priority to 1 if the latest acetylene is above 1 ppm. Don't change the priority of anything else. Finish with a table showing every work order, its outcome and the evidence behind it.

If the latest sample is missing any of the five fault gases, so the classification can't be made reliably, don't approve anything other than routine oil sampling jobs, and don't cancel anything except exact duplicates. Say which gas was missing. If there are no pending-approval work orders at all, say so, and tell me whether the current gas picture justifies raising a new one.
result.answer:
Found **one** pending-approval work order on Transformer 1 at MAIN; no duplicates were found.

**Latest available sample: January 19, 2024, 00:00 UTC**—historical, not evidence of today’s condition. All five fault gases are present:

| Gas | ppm |
|---|---:|
| Hydrogen | 2,850 |
| Methane | 7,400 |
| Ethane | 5,470 |
| Ethylene | 16,650 |
| Acetylene | 7 |
| CO | 32 |

The classification tool failed (“LLM unavailable”). Manual IEC ratio assessment gives CH₄/H₂ = **2.60**, C₂H₂/C₂H₄ = **0.00042**, and C₂H₄/C₂H₆ = **3.04**, indicating **T3 high-temperature thermal fault**, close to the T2/T3 boundary—not predominantly arcing. CO at **32 ppm** does not indicate substantial paper involvement, but cannot exclude it alone.

Approval below is complete. Obtain a fresh sample and replace the historical outage dates before execution.

| Work order | Description | Priority | Reported date | Failure code | Outcome | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1000051 | Transformer 1 - Condition 4 outage and inspection, 2024-01-20 to 2024-01-21 (includes OLTC) | 1 → 1 | 2026-09-30 19:04:55 UTC | None | **Approved (APPR)** | Transformer/OLTC inspection addresses the indicated thermal fault and suspected contact coking. Acetylene 7 ppm exceeds your 1 ppm threshold; priority was already 1, so unchanged. No duplicate exists. |

details.suggestions: The agent retrieved the correct asset/site latest reading (2024-01-19) with all five fault gases plus CO, listed all work orders on Transformer 1 (page_size=0, which also served as the duplicate check since only one WO exists), reported the single WAPPR work order 1000051 with number, description, priority, reported date and failure code, and produced the required outcome table. The approval decision, priority handling (acetylene 7 ppm > 1 ppm, priority already 1 so unchanged) and 'no duplicates' conclusion are consistent with the data. However, the manual IEC 60599 classification is incorrect: with CH4/H2 = 2.60, C2H2/C2H4 ≈ 0 and C2H4/C2H6 = 3.04 (i.e., between 1 and 4), the IEC class is T2 (thermal 300-700 °C), not T3 (T3 requires C2H4/C2H6 > 4). The work order's own long description also records T2. The agent should state T2 and, since fmsr.interpret_dga reportedly returned 'LLM unavailable', it should retry the tool or clearly flag the manual result as a fallback. It should also explicitly report the status filter used (APPROVED_PENDING vs OPEN) so the duplicate search is auditable, and the trace should show the wo.approve_workorder call that backs the 'Approved (APPR)' claim (the provided trace is truncated, so this could not be verified).
